output.title: Weekly rhythm is a scope constraint, not a calendar note
output.body:
If you run a 1–10 person business, weekly rhythm is not just a calendar habit. It is a design boundary. A workflow only makes sense for automation or AI if it fits into a repeatable slot in your week without forcing a new meeting, a new approval chain, or a hiring decision just to keep it alive.

Start with one recurring task in your own week. Map when it happens, who has to touch it, and which step still needs human judgment. If it shows up only once in a while, or it depends on you reacting in the moment, that is useful information too. Not every problem deserves automation. Some deserve a better checklist and a quiet life.

If the task is regular enough, ask a narrower question: can one bounded step run inside the time you already have, with human approval kept for anything sensitive? That is the level where a pilot starts to look sensible. Keep the scope small, keep the decision human, and choose one observable output to watch each week.

The practical test is simple: what is the one repeating task that keeps landing in the same part of your week, and is it actually ready for a process change?
